title: UKPNP Delegation Meets Baroness Emma Nicholson in London to Discuss Kashmir Crisis and Political Developments
excerpt: A high level UKPNP delegation led by Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri held a meeting with Baroness Emma Nicholson in London to discuss the Kashmir conflict and political developments across the region.
author: Special Correspondent

heroImage.caption: UKPNP delegation meeting Baroness Emma Nicholson in London.

items: UKPNP delegation met Baroness Emma Nicholson in London House of Lords
Delegation discussed the Kashmir conflict and developments across all regions
The 2007 European Parliament Kashmir Report highlighted as key international document
Concerns raised about political rights and constitutional developments
Call made for renewed international engagement on Kashmir

body.text: A high level delegation of the United Kashmir People’s National Party, UKPNP, led by its Exiled Chairman Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri held a formal meeting and briefing with Baroness Emma Nicholson, Member of the House of Lords of the United Kingdom.

body.caption: Members of the UKPNP delegation during the meeting in London.

body.text: The meeting focused on political conditions in the historical State of Jammu and Kashmir and recent developments affecting the region. Baroness Nicholson has long been associated with international engagement on Kashmir and previously served as Rapporteur on Kashmir in the European Parliament.

The UKPNP delegation included Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan, Central Spokesperson UKPNP, Mahmood Kashmiri, Member Central Committee UKPNP, Sardar Tikka Khan Tahir, Central Secretary Information UKPNP, Sardar Amjad Yousaf, President UKPNP Europe Zone, Sardar Tariq Khan, President UKPNP UK Zone, Raja Sarfraz, General Secretary UKPNP UK Zone and Sajjad Hussain, President UKPNP London.
During the meeting the delegation compared the findings of the 2007 European Parliament report with current developments across Jammu, Kashmir, Ladakh, Gilgit Baltistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
The people of Jammu and Kashmir must remain central to any political process regarding the future of the region.

The delegation explained that Indian administered Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh held a special constitutional status until August 2019 when the Government of India abrogated Article 370 and Article 35A and reorganised the region into two union territories.

While Indian administered regions have stronger infrastructure and democratic institutions, the delegation said the constitutional changes created concerns about democratic representation and political rights.
Situation in Azad Kashmir and Gilgit Baltistan

The delegation informed Baroness Nicholson that Azad Kashmir and Gilgit Baltistan remain under strong administrative control from Islamabad and lack representation in Pakistan’s National Assembly and Senate.
They said nationalist political parties face restrictions and candidates must sign declarations supporting accession to Pakistan before participating in elections.
There is no military solution to the Kashmir conflict. Dialogue and respect for human rights remain essential.
The delegation stressed that the State of Jammu and Kashmir historically existed as a single political entity until 1947 and remains one of the longest unresolved international disputes.
UKPNP leaders called for renewed international engagement based on United Nations resolutions and recommendations of the European Parliament report.
Baroness Nicholson welcomed the briefing and expressed readiness to continue discussions and engagement on the Kashmir issue.
